item.text: The first recording is fully mapped. It is a mug-pizza preparation with several omissions and out-of-order actions: the cook adds baking soda but appears to skip baking powder, mixes once before adding milk and again afterward, and briefly microwaves the mug near the end. I’m saving this complete first transcript before moving to the remaining clips.

item.text: A major ambiguity is now resolved from full-resolution checks: I is not a fourth mug-pizza recording; it is an improvised pour-over coffee recording. The long late action is grounds being spooned into a filter, followed by a small bloom pour, an extended wait, and the remaining water. I’m correcting the grouping before saving it so those motions receive coffee labels rather than visually similar mug labels.

The coffee recordings diverge sharply. L repeatedly checks the water temperature during a prolonged pour, while M never reaches a normal pour-over: it re-weighs spilled beans, folds filters multiple times, measures water late, and ultimately discards the grounds. I’m recording those repeated checks/folds and omitting nominal pour steps that are not visibly carried out.

The three egg-tortilla recordings are now saved. They include the visibly repeated whisk/stir passes around microwave interruptions; I have not invented microwave labels for those intervals because the closed vocabulary has no egg-microwave step. The remaining work is the three nut-butter pinwheel recordings and three corn recordings, followed by JSON validation.

The pinwheel recordings are saved with separate entries for each visibly distinct floss-slicing pass, including S’s prolonged series of extra slices. I’m on the final corn trio now; T uses two microwave passes with seasoning and lime added only after the second pass.

item.text: I’ve reduced the remaining work to the three corn recordings. T and U show repeated microwave/season/mix cycles, so I’m checking V at two-second resolution before saving all three together; this is where coarse sampling would most easily collapse genuinely repeated steps.

The high-resolution checks resolved the ambiguity: U has exactly two microwave runs, not three. The second was set to two minutes even though its closed-vocabulary label is “3 more minutes,” so I’ll preserve the action label but use the actual observed interval. I’m now separating the short seasoning additions that occur between those two runs.

T is the deliberately messy corn run: the cook skipped thawing, seasoned before heating, set the only microwave pass to about three minutes, then added butter, salt, and extracted lime only afterward. I’m correcting the saved T block to reflect that actual order and removing the second microwave step that coarse sampling had falsely suggested.
